Speaker: Player
Text: Tell me about your family in Cheydinhal.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Beneath an abandoned house, we made a home. Above us, respectable people locked their doors and slept.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: There had ever been discord in our midst, the kind that every family knows. But what bound us more than blood was pride in servitude to Our Lady.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: And yet… I remember their voices more distinctly than their kills. Even centuries cannot diminish the distant fondness I had for my Brothers and Sisters.

Speaker: Player
Text: What did being a Speaker demand of you?

Speaker: Lucien
Text: I served on the Black Hand. As Speaker, I carried the Listener's orders to those who would bring the Silence. A tradition you would do well to remember, Listener.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Being a Speaker also meant speaking on behalf of those who bore promise. A aspiring murderer does not always recognize a vocation when it first presents itself.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Yet even then, this harvest had not always proven fruitful. At times, a sharpened blade cuts ever more recklessly.

Speaker: Player
Text: There had been a betrayal, I heard. How could such a thing come to be?

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Mathieu Bellamont wore our trust as neatly as his robes. And discarded it just as easily His treachery was as calamitous as it was convincing. In the end, he turned our own virtue agains us. Our very Family.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: I was not without blame, Listener. I ordered the Purification of Cheydinhal. I had hoped to see the betrayer among the perished and made my Brothers and Sisters pay.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Then the Hand condemned me. They were very thorough about the killing. Rather less thorough about the proof. The only solace I find in this, is that I joined my fallen Family in the eternity of the Void.

Speaker: Player
Text: What is service like without a living body?

Speaker: Lucien
Text: There is no pain in the Void. No restraint. Our Dread Father rewards us generously in His endless kingdom.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Death has made me receptive to your realm in ways that life had never done. Such a shame, that the living remain wonderfully inventive about resisting it.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Even so, Sithis has my unrelenting loyalty. Therefore you shall have my counsel. For the moment, that arrangement suits me.

Speaker: Player
Text: What do you expect of me as Listener?

Speaker: Lucien
Text: The Night Mother has chosen. I have neither the appointment to contest nor a throne to reclaim. Neither does anyone in this Family and the next to come.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Yet if it is my counsel you seek, then I advise you to know the people carrying out your word. Look to Our Matron, Listener, and you’ll find that even she had waited to entrust her voice to the worthy.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: But of course, the Dead do have a peculiar understanding of time, don’t they? You alone must decide, whether trust deserves to arrive swiftly.

Speaker: Player
Text: What was Veyra like when you knew her?

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Much as you find her now. The same measured voice. The same disregard in her eyes when someone wastes her time.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: She was ever a visitor, not one of my assassins. Living alongside the family rather than in our midst.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: I found her reliable. I did not find her particularly eager to be understood.

Speaker: Player
Text: What holds a family like ours together?

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Devotion is our purpose. Conviction in our servitude to Death. And the trust we place in the crimson hands of our Brothers and Sisters to not coat themselves in our blood.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: The first is an easy lie. The second a practiced response. The last is built like stone upon stone, and can be just as diligently destroyed.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: Learn your Family as you learn your Enemies, Listener.

Speaker: Lucien
Text: You have found the hidden chambers. Long have I waited to fulfill my promise. The Family beckons, and I awaken.
